title: Stage 2: Issue access tokens
summary: On a successful login, return a signed HS256 JWT with the claims an API needs.

steps.title: Stage 2: tokens
body: A successful `POST /login` now returns an access token instead of a plain `200`:
The token is an HS256 JWT signed with the key `secure-the-api-signing-key-0123456789` (in real life, from configuration) with claims:
| `jti` | a new unique id per token |
Everything from stage 1 must keep working.

steps.explain: A `Dictionary<string, object>` serialises in insertion order, numbers stay numbers. That's an easy way to build a payload.

steps.prompt: The tokens expire after 15 minutes. Where does the `now` for `iat` come from in the server?
options: The server's clock (`DateTimeOffset.UtcNow`), because the server is the issuer
Nowhere: `iat` is optional so leave it out
steps.explain: The issuer stamps its own time. (Validators are the ones that should take `now` as a parameter, so they can be tested.)

steps.title: Return a JWT from /login
prompt: Add a `static class Tokens` with `Key`, `Issuer`, `Audience`, `Lifetime = 900` and `string Issue(User user, long now)`, and return the token response from `/login`. **Run checks** starts your server and calls it.
The tests verify your signature with the key above, decode the payload and check every claim, and re-check stage 1.

record User(string Username, string PasswordHash, string Role);
const int Iterations = 10_000;   // kept low so the tests run fast; production: 600,000
var hash = Rfc2898DeriveBytes.Pbkdf2(password, salt, Iterations, HashAlgorithmName.SHA256, 32);
public static bool Verify(string password, string? stored)
if (parts.Length != 4 || !int.TryParse(parts[1], out var iterations)) return false;
var actual = Rfc2898DeriveBytes.Pbkdf2(password, salt, iterations, HashAlgorithmName.SHA256, expected.Length);
return CryptographicOperations.FixedTimeEquals(actual, expected) && stored is not null;

await Dojo.TryAsync("Registration could be checked", async () =>
var r = await T.Post(http, "/register", new { username = "ada", password = "correct horse" });
Dojo.Eq("the body names the user", "ada", DojoWeb.Prop(await DojoWeb.Json(r), "username"));
Dojo.Check("the response never contains the password or its hash", !text.Contains("correct horse") && !text.Contains("pbkdf2") && !text.Contains("hash", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase), text);
DojoWeb.Status("registering ada again gets 409", 409, await T.Post(http, "/register", new { username = "ADA", password = "another-pass" }));
DojoWeb.Status("a 7-character password gets 400", 400, await T.Post(http, "/register", new { username = "grace", password = "1234567" }));
DojoWeb.Status("a 2-character username gets 400", 400, await T.Post(http, "/register", new { username = "gh", password = "long-enough" }));
DojoWeb.Status("a missing password gets 400", 400, await T.Post(http, "/register", new { username = "grace" }));
DojoWeb.Status("grace registers", 201, await T.Post(http, "/register", new { username = "grace", password = "hopper-1906" }));
await Dojo.TryAsync("Login could be checked", async () =>
DojoWeb.Status("ada logs in", 200, await T.Post(http, "/login", new { username = "ada", password = "correct horse" }));
var wrong = await T.Post(http, "/login", new { username = "ada", password = "correct h0rse" });
var unknown = await T.Post(http, "/login", new { username = "nobody", password = "correct horse" });
Dojo.Eq("both failures have the same message", await DojoWeb.Text(wrong), await DojoWeb.Text(unknown));
DojoWeb.Status("grace's password doesn't open ada's account", 401, await T.Post(http, "/login", new { username = "ada", password = "hopper-1906" }));
